stories.headline: Cyclone threat looms over Bay of Bengal, fishermen put on alert
stories.title: Cyclone threat looms over Bay of Bengal, fishermen put on alert
stories.summary: Chennai, Oct 24 : Fishermen were on Saturday advised against venturing into the open sea for five days from Sunday as a cyclonic storm is expected to develop over the Bay of Bengal, according to a weather advisory. Several districts of Tamil Nadu are also likely to receive heavy rain accompanied by thunderstorms and gusty winds. The Chennai weather department, in its bulletin, said a weather system over the Comorin region and adjoining southern Tamil Nadu and Kerala on October 22 had shifted towards the southeastern Arabian Sea and neighbouring Lakshadweep region by 8.30 a.m. on October 23. An associated atmospheric trough extending towards the northern Tamil Nadu coast through Kerala, at about 1.5 kms above sea level, was influencing rainfall across the region. For October 24, heavy rain was forecast at isolated places in Tirunelveli and Kanyakumari districts and the hill areas of Coimbatore, the Nilgiris and Theni. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40–50 kmph were also predicted. Rain was expected across several other districts, including Erode, Salem, Namakkal, Karur, Tiruchirappalli, Tenkasi, Madurai, Dindigul, Virudhunagar and Tiruppur. Chennai and its neighbouring districts, the delta region, Puducherry and Karaikal were also expected to experience showers. On October 25, isolated heavy rainfall is likely in the Nilgiris, Coimbatore, Theni, Dindigul, Madurai, Perambalur, Ariyalur and Tiruchirappalli. Thunderstorms and gusty winds may accompany rainfall in Sivaganga, Pudukkottai, Ramanathapuram, Tirupattur, Krishnagiri, Dharmapuri, Tiruvannamalai, Vellore and Ranipet, besides several western and northern districts. Rain is also forecast for Chennai, Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Tiruvallur, Cuddalore and parts of the Cauvery delta. The department forecast a further spell of intense rain on October 26, with isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall likely in the Nilgiris, Coimbatore, Theni, Madurai, Sivaganga, Ramanathapuram and Pudukkottai. Other districts, including Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai, Erode, Salem, Namakkal, Karur, Tiruppur, Dindigul and Virudhunagar, could also receive heavy showers. Rain accompanied by thunder, lightning and winds of 40–50 kmph is expected in parts of Thoothukudi, Perambalur, Ariyalur, Kallakurichi, Cuddalore and Tiruvannamalai, as well as Puducherry and Karaikal. Elsewhere in Tamil Nadu, moderate rainfall is likely at varying numbers of locations during the three-day forecast period. The five-day warning for fishermen begins on Sunday and extends through Thursday, October 29. The advisory links the restriction to the anticipated development of the Bay of Bengal weather system. —IANS

stories.headline: PIL in SC seeks expert panel to examine election commission’s functioning, curb religious appeals in campaigns
stories.title: PIL in SC seeks expert panel to examine election commission’s functioning, curb religious appeals in campaigns
stories.summary: The objections reportedly concerned changes to statutory Form 6 without authorisation, centralisation of the electoral database, the filing of appeals in West Bengal without approval and orders relating to the allocation of work
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A PIL has been filed in the Supreme Court seeking an independent expert committee, headed by a former Chief Justice of India or a former Supreme Court judge, to examine alleged institutional deficiencies in the functioning of the Election Commission of India (ECI).

Filed by advocate Vishal Tiwari, the petition has also sought a direction prohibiting the Election Commission from allowing candidates and political parties to invoke religious identities, display religious symbols or make communal and sectarian appeals, including through hate speech, while campaigning for elections.

The petition refers to a September 23 newspaper report which stated that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded written objections on at least 14 occasions over a period of ten months against decisions allegedly taken unilaterally by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The objections reportedly concerned changes to statutory Form 6 without authorisation, centralisation of the electoral database, the filing of appeals in West Bengal without approval and orders relating to the allocation of work.
According to the plea, the ECI acknowledged the dissenting notes but characterised them as routine suggestions, without explaining who had authorised the changes to Form 6.
The petition has also raised concerns over the implementation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal.

Referring to media reports on an affidavit filed by the ECI, it stated that around 38.20 lakh appeals had been filed by people excluded from the electoral rolls, while only approximately 1.02 lakh had been disposed of.
The poll body reportedly sought to increase the number of appellate tribunals from 19 to 42.
Separately, the plea cited a media report stating that 2,70,313 electors in Maharashtra's draft electoral roll were recorded as being between 101 and 150 years old due to a default birth-year glitch.

Arguing that these developments warrant an institutional review, the petitioner has sought the constitution of a committee comprising specialists in constitutional law, election administration, statistics, technology, cybersecurity and data protection.

The proposed panel would examine systemic shortcomings in the ECI's functioning, with the plea seeking measures to strengthen institutional accountability and safeguard the integrity of the electoral process.

Emphasising the prospective and non-partisan nature of the plea, Tiwari has clarified that it neither seeks to attribute wrongdoing to any political party or public office-holder nor challenges the outcome of any election.

stories.headline: Operation Sindoor features in Trump's midterm poll rallies, regrets no Nobel for efforts
stories.title: Operation Sindoor features in Trump's midterm poll rallies, regrets no Nobel for efforts
stories.summary: Washington, Oct 24: India’s Operation Sindoor has featured in election rallies for the US midterm elections, with President Donald Trump once again claiming to have stopped two nuclear-armed neighbours from going to war by threatening them with steep tariffs. India launched Operation Sindoor in May 2025, targeting terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK) following the April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam, which claimed several lives. Addressing an election rally in Florida on Friday, Trump once again took credit for stopping India and Pakistan from escalating their war last year by threatening them with steep tariffs. He said the two nuclear-armed nations were angry but stopped shooting, adding that “eleven planes were shot.” “You stop India and Pakistan, two nuclear nations... I said, 'Fellas, if you guys are going to do that, you're not going to trade with the United States...I'm going to put massive tariffs on both of you, 250 per cent, so you won't be able to do any business'," Trump said. He said India and Pakistan were very upset and very angry, but they stopped shooting, and the war was over. “Eleven planes were shot. I stopped all these wars, and it's really an honour to do so..." Trump said, adding he did not get any help from the United Nations in this effort. “I'd never made one phone call to the United Nations. But we got them all stopped, and a couple more left. I had no idea when I was running, I had no idea that they had so many wars,” Trump said. Trump also expressed disappointment over not receiving the Nobel Peace Prize for his claimed diplomatic interventions. "I've settled eight wars. Did I get the Nobel Prize? No," he said. India has repeatedly rejected Trump's assertions that he brokered a ceasefire between New Delhi and Islamabad, maintaining that the understanding to stop military action was reached directly between the two countries. After Indian strikes targeted key terror launchpads, military action was paused on May 10 following a request from Pakistan, according to India's account of the developments.

stories.headline: India secure 4-2 victory over Laos in U15 World Cup opener
stories.title: India secure 4-2 victory over Laos in U15 World Cup opener
stories.summary: Baku, Oct 24 : India began their campaign at the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup & Festival Azerbaijan 2026 on a high note, registering a dominant 4-2 victory over Laos in their Group K opener at the Hovsan Competition Complex Pitch 1B in Baku on Saturday. India's Captain Macdonnish Ngairangbam (7') and R Lalremruatfela (11') handed the team an early two-goal advantage before Anavin Xayyasone (12') halved the deficit for Laos. Souksavanh Siliseng (24') equalised for the Southeast Asians soon after half-time, but India finished strong, with Lalremruatfela (31') and Soumojit Sarkar (33') firing from long range to restore the lead and secure the nation's first three points at a FIFA tournament. The tournament features 189 national teams divided into 32 groups, with matches played in an eight-a-side format. Each match consists of two 20-minute halves, with rolling substitutions permitted. Bibiano Fernandes' team made a bright start and created two chances in the opening four minutes. A powerful left-footed effort from inside the box by Deepak Singh Arambam was pushed away by the Laos goalkeeper Anousith Souksavanh in the third minute, before Macdonnish was denied by the advancing custodian a minute later. India took the lead in the seventh minute after brilliant footwork from Deepak, who worked his way into the small box before cutting the ball back for Macdonnish to tap home. The pressure continued to pay off, with India doubling their advantage in the 11th minute. A Laos clearance was blocked by Deepak, and the ball fell to R Lalremruatfela, who took a touch before slamming home with his left boot. Laos responded almost immediately, pulling a goal back in the 12th minute through Anavin Xayyasone, whose long-range effort left India goalkeeper Jenit Ningthoujam rooted to the spot. The tempo dropped following the early flurry of goals, with neither side creating a clear-cut opportunity before the five-minute half-time break. India threatened again after the restart, with a header from Macdonnish drifting inches wide following a corner in the 21st minute. Laos, however, drew level three minutes later when Souksavanh Siliseng struck the first time from outside the box, finding the bottom corner. The equaliser prompted India to raise their intensity, with much of the play taking place in the Laos half. India regained the lead in the 31st minute, with R Lalremruatfela collecting a pass from Soumojit Sarkar before firing left-footed into the far corner from outside the box to make it 3-2. India extended their advantage in the 33rd minute when Sarkar struck from just inside the halfway line, sending the ball over the goalkeeper and into the net. The young Indian side managed the remainder of the match well to preserve their two-goal advantage and secure all three points. India will next face Cameroon on Sunday before taking on Grenada later the same day. They will conclude the qualification stage against Bahrain and Senegal on October 26. Their results across the five matches will determine which performance tier they enter for the second phase. --IANS

stories.headline: Cabinet Sub-Committee seeks to draw up department-wise plan to tackle El Nino induced drought conditions
stories.title: Cabinet Sub-Committee seeks to draw up department-wise plan to tackle El Nino induced drought conditions
stories.summary: 358 mandals provisionally identified as drought-affected based on rainfall, crop coverage
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Cabinet Sub-Committee on Drought and El Nino conditions chaired by Deputy Chief Minister M. Bhatti Vikramarka on Friday resolved to prepare a comprehensive and department-wise action plan to tackle the drought caused by El Nino conditions.

The plans will focus on safeguarding supply of water for drinking and irrigation and ensuring uninterrupted electricity, agricultural support and rural employment so that people do not face hardships in the coming days.

The first meeting of the Cabinet Sub-Committee, constituted to review the drought and El Nino situation in the State and recommend appropriate measures to the government, was held here on Friday (October 23).
The meeting primarily discussed the impact of El Nino and drought in various parts of the State, water availability, relief measures for farmers and future action plans.

Sub-Committee members and Ministers N. Uttam Kumar Reddy, Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy, D. Seethakka, Tummala Nageswara Rao and Vakiti Srihari along with Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju and secretaries of the concerned departments attended the meeting.
Mr. Vikramarka asked the officials to scientifically assess drought conditions and examine the mandals eligible for declaration as drought-affected areas under the prescribed guidelines.
He stressed that the government’s priority was to minimise the impact of drought and ensure timely delivery of necessary assistance to people through coordinated efforts.
He instructed officials to assess not only areas already experiencing severe drought but also mandals where the drought impact exceeds 20%.
An advance assessment of the likely impact of drought on various sectors would help the government provide timely assistance to those in need, he said.
He suggested that every department identify the challenges and prepare a clear action plan to address them.
He asked the officials to anticipate challenges in the power sector arising from El Nino conditions and take measures in advance.
Mr. Uttam Kumar Reddy asked the District Collectors to conduct weekly review meetings with the officials concerned to monitor the measures being implemented to address the drought conditions.

article_sentences: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Government of India, on Saturday ordered the transfer of senior IAS officer Dr Sajjan Singh Yadav to Jammu and Kashmir and posted him as Chief Secretary of the Union Territory.
Srinagar: Dr Sajjan Singh Yadav, IAS officer (AGMUT, 1995), has been appointed as the new chief secretary of Jammu and Kashmir.
As per an order issued from Kartavya Bhavan-3, New Delhi, Dr Sajjan Singh Yadav, IAS (AGMUT:1995), has been transferred from Delhi to Jammu and Kashmir.

"With the approval of the Competent Authority, Dr Sajjan Singh Yadav, IAS (AGMUT:1995) is hereby transferred from Delhi to Jammu & Kashmir and posted as Chief Secretary, Jammu & Kashmir w.e.f. 01.11.2026 or from the date of joining, whichever is later," reads the order dated 24th October, 2026.
Sajjan Singh Yadav, born on January 5, 1969, is a 1995 batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre.
He has been serving as Additional Chief Secretary and CEO, New Delhi, Delhi Jal Board since June 9, 2026.

His educational qualifications include an M.P.A. in Public Policy from the Hubert Humphrey School of Public Policy, an M.B.A. in Finance from Delhi University, and an M.P.A. in Economics from Harvard University.
He is also a successful author, best known for his books on India's vaccine history and the success stories of UPSC aspirants.

Throughout his career, Sajjan Singh Yadav has held various positions such as Special Secretary, Additional Secretary, Finance Commissioner, Commissioner, CEO, Secretary, Joint Secretary, Director, Deputy Secretary, and Private Secretary.
He is proficient in English and Hindi.
The present chief secretary, Atul Dulloo, IAS (AGMUT: 1989), is retiring on October 31, 2026.

Srinagar: Dr Sajjan Singh Yadav, IAS officer (AGMUT, 1995), has been appointed as the new chief secretary of Jammu and Kashmir.
body: As per an order issued from Kartavya Bhavan-3, New Delhi, Dr Sajjan Singh Yadav, IAS (AGMUT:1995), has been transferred from Delhi to Jammu and Kashmir.

"With the approval of the Competent Authority, Dr Sajjan Singh Yadav, IAS (AGMUT:1995) is hereby transferred from Delhi to Jammu & Kashmir and posted as Chief Secretary, Jammu & Kashmir w.e.f. 01.11.2026 or from the date of joining, whichever is later," reads the order dated 24th October, 2026.
Sajjan Singh Yadav, born on January 5, 1969, is a 1995 batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre.
He has been serving as Additional Chief Secretary and CEO, New Delhi, Delhi Jal Board since June 9, 2026.

His educational qualifications include an M.P.A. in Public Policy from the Hubert Humphrey School of Public Policy, an M.B.A. in Finance from Delhi University, and an M.P.A. in Economics from Harvard University.
He is also a successful author, best known for his books on India's vaccine history and the success stories of UPSC aspirants.

Throughout his career, Sajjan Singh Yadav has held various positions such as Special Secretary, Additional Secretary, Finance Commissioner, Commissioner, CEO, Secretary, Joint Secretary, Director, Deputy Secretary, and Private Secretary.
He is proficient in English and Hindi.

article_sentences: New Delhi: Two India U-19 women’s sides will take on Nepal in a tri-series at the BCCI’s Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru from November 10 to 22, as the two-time defending champions look to enter the final leg of preparations ahead of next year’s U19 World Cup.

According to a press release issued by Cricket Association of Nepal (CAN) secretary Paras Khadka, the series will feature India U-19 Women’s ‘A’ and India U-19 Women’s ‘B’ alongside Nepal’s U-19 women’s team.
India U-19 ‘B’ team will first take on Nepal on November 12, before the visitors face India ‘A’ side on November 14.
India U-19 ‘B’ team will take on Nepal in the first reverse fixture of November 18, before India U-19 ‘A’ take on the visitors on November 20.
The tri-series will conclude with the final on November 22, with all matches having 1pm start time.

stories.headline: Gold, silver prices drop sharply as oil prices surge
stories.title: Gold, silver prices drop sharply as oil prices surge
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 24 : Gold prices dipped 3.28 per cent on a weekly basis, while silver prices declined 7.83 per cent this week, as rising crude oil prices heightened inflation fears. The rising inflation concerns reinforced expectations that global interest rates will stay higher for longer, prompting a wave of selling across precious‑metals markets. On Friday, MCX gold futures expiring December declined 0.81 per cent while MCX silver futures for December shed 1.75 per cent. Gold futures stood at Rs 1,42,150, while silver futures stood at Rs 1,96,100 per kg. Gold saw its steepest weekly decline since June and slipped below the psychologically important $4,000 per ounce level for the first time since mid-July, analysts said. The selloff in silver intensified over weakness in US technology stocks, particularly AI-linked companies, which triggered margin calls and forced investors to liquidate precious-metal holdings. Meanwhile, crude oil surged to multi-month highs following renewed attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and shipping routes, while the Indian rupee surrendered its early-week gains amid rising oil prices and renewed dollar demand. However, lower prices encouraged physical gold purchases in India during the Dussehra festival, providing some underlying demand support, while Chinese jewellery demand remained subdued. Market participants forecast that precious metals could remain under pressure if elevated energy prices reinforce inflation concerns and expectations of tighter monetary policy. However, physical demand and any moderation in bond yields could offer support following the recent correction, they said. Markets largely expect the US Fed to keep interest rates unchanged at the October 27–28 policy meeting, but expectations of another rate hike in December remain elevated, with traders pricing approximately a 78 per cent probability. Investors are also awaiting the US Personal Consumption Expenditures report next week for additional guidance on inflation and future interest-rate decisions. Immediate resistance for Comex Gold is placed at $4,070–$4,100 zone, while support lies at $3,970–$4,000 zone, analysts said. For MCX Gold, immediate resistance is placed at Rs 1,43,000–Rs 1,43,700 zone, while the support lies at Rs 1,40,000–Rs 1,41,000, they added. —IANS aar/na

stories.headline: How to Compare the Home Solar Panel Companies in India
stories.title: How to Compare the Home Solar Panel Companies in India
stories.summary: Rooftop solar is one of the smartest moves a homeowner can make right now, and three things explain why. Electricity bills keep rising, so the savings from solar grow every year. At the same time, the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana brings down what you pay at the end through subsidies. Financing has also become easier, so you don't need to pay the full cost at once. All of this has pushed solar into the mainstream. But with that demand has come a flood of solar companies. Almost every one of them promises the lowest price, the fastest installation, and the biggest savings. On a sales call, most of them sound the same. Here's the problem. You won't know which company was actually right until months after the solar system installation, when your electricity bill either drops the way you were promised, or barely moves at all. A solar system sits on your roof for close to 25 years. So, comparing companies properly, before you sign anything, matters a lot more than people realise. Here's how to actually do it. How to Compare the Home Solar Panel Companies in India To find the right solar panels for your home , it is crucial to keep certain things in mind to get the optimal results. You can check the following factors before saying yes to any solar company: 1. Start With Certification Before anything else, check if a company only installs BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards)-certified panels that are listed under ALMM (Approved List of Models and Manufacturers). This isn't a small detail. ALMM listing is what makes your system eligible for the PM Surya Ghar Yojana. BIS certification confirms the panels meet India's official safety standards. Ask for this in writing. A company actually using certified equipment will hand over the paperwork without any hesitation. 2. Compare Their Track Record Ask each company how long they've been installing rooftop solar, and how many homes they've actually worked on. A company with more years has likely dealt with tricky roof shapes, local shading problems, and weather patterns specific to different parts of India. You can also check a company's number of installations directly on the PM Surya Ghar portal. 3. Check Whether They Assess Your Roof Before Quoting A professional solar company sends someone to your home before giving you a final number. This visit should include a proper roof analysis, checking the roof's load-bearing capacity, taking exact measurements, mapping shadows across different seasons, and giving you a custom layout of where each panel will go. If a company hands you a quote without ever seeing your roof, that number is a guess. It isn't a real assessment, and you shouldn't treat it like one. 4. Find Out Who Actually Installs the System Many solar companies handle sales themselves, then hand off the physical installation to local solar companies. Ask directly whether the company uses its own trained Solar experts or outsources the job. This matters more than people expect. The equipment might be identical across two companies, but the quality of the installation rarely is. 5. Compare the Quotes Line by Line A trustworthy company gives you an itemised quote, not just one vague total. It should break down the cost of panels, inverter, mounting structure, wiring, and labour separately. If a quote feels vague or incomplete, take that as a warning sign. It often means hidden costs later, or corners cut on equipment quality. 6. Look at the Panel Technology Being Offered By 2026, newer panel types like Mono-PERC and N-Type TOPCon have become common. They offer better efficiency and degrade more slowly over time. Ask each company what kind of panels they're actually using, and whether that matches current technology. A company that stays updated usually cares more about your system's long-term performance than the one who’s simply selling whatever's cheapest to source. 7. Ask Who Handles the Subsidy and Net Metering Paperwork Applying for the PM Surya Ghar Yojana and setting up net metering means dealing with government portals and your local DISCOM (Distribution Company). For a first-timer, this can get confusing fast. A good company manages this entire process for you, instead of leaving you to chase approvals on your own. This single factor can make the difference between a smooth experience and a stressful one while getting the solar system installed. 8. Look for a Written Performance Guarantee This is where most companies fall short. Ask if there's a written commitment on how many units your system is expected to generate each year, and what happens if it falls short. Very few companies are willing to put this in writing. A company called SolarSquare, now operating in various cities across India, backs their installations with a savings guarantee, offering compensation if the system generates fewer units than promised. 9. Check What After-Sales Support Actually Covers A reliable solar company doesn't disappear after installation. Panels need occasional servicing and preventive system checks that catch small issues before they turn expensive. Ask exactly how many servicing visits are included in their plan, over what period, and what's actually covered under that plan. A company offering a real, structured service contract is telling you something important. They expect to stay accountable for years after your system is commissioned, not just until the payment clears. 10. Read Beyond the Star Ratings A high star rating alone doesn't tell you much. Look for detailed reviews instead, especially ones written months or years after installation. That's usually where the real differences between companies show up. You can also ask any company for a reference visit to a nearby customer's home, to get an honest sense of how they handle things once the sale is done. How to Put This Comparison Together Once you've checked all of this across two or three companies, line up their answers side by side. ● Who's certified and ALMM-listed? ● Who actually visited your roof? ● Who gave you a clear, itemised quote? ● Who's willing to put a performance guarantee in writing? Among solar providers operating in India, “SolarSquare” is the #1 rooftop home solar company in India as per the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana portal. The company uses only BIS and ALMM-certified panels, and its mounting structures are engineered to withstand wind speeds of up to 170 km/hr. Their mounting structure, called “WindPro Mount™ 2.0”, is also IIT-Bombay approved. It also runs a structured solar servicing & maintenance program with remote monitoring, rather than treating installation as a one-time job. Final Thoughts Comparing solar companies in India was never about finding whoever quotes the lowest price or gives the smoothest sales pitch. It comes down to certified equipment, a proper roof assessment, transparent pricing, a written performance guarantee, and real after-sales support. Those panels are going to sit on your roof for close to 25 years. Take the time to compare properly before you sign anything. It's really what separates a solar investment that pays off from one that quietly lets you down. (The views, opinions, and claims in this article are solely those of the author’s and do not represent the editorial stance of The Assam Tribune)
